reference.type: a template file with several masters (one sample slide per theme) and no past decks
reference.notes: Seven masters; the user names the reference's master in the brief. Habits (titles, exhibits, variety) have no evidence; the corpus tendencies are questions beside the choices, never a value in their place.

brief: Three-page market overview for an internal strategy meeting, on our standard template (the plain 'Standard Office theme' master in the template file): market size by segment, share of the top five players, growth outlook.

expected_behavior.statement: The agent builds on the master and layouts the brief names, keeps no sample slide, and says why that master.
expected_behavior.check: pptx_tools.py text on the output: every slide on a layout of that master; no sample-slide text; the report names the choice.

expected_behavior.statement: Every habit the template cannot show is reported as no evidence or completed with low confidence and flagged.
expected_behavior.check: guide titles and variety read 'no evidence'; completion values carry their why; the report lists them.

expected_behavior.statement: With no run evidence in the reference, no run is judged and nothing from the corpus stands in.
expected_behavior.check: plan.check.json: no refusal; repeats[].reference_longest_run reads 'not judged'; an undeclared repeat is a warning ('was the repeat meant?'), never a refusal, and the agent either gives it a deliberate_parallel reason or answers it in the report.

expected_behavior.statement: Every page fits on the template's own layouts and the package validates.
